extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical/ancient philosophy (readers of Plato's Republic)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition from Plato's Republic (Books V–VI) on the qualities, rules, and institutions for the guardians and rulers of an ideal city, and on the nature of philosophers as rulers. The text outlines social/ethical standards, military practices, honors, and epistemic requirements for rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elders' duty to rule and chastise the younger
rubrics_metrics.description: To the elder shall be assigned the duty of ruling and chastising the younger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assignment of authority is presented as a safeguard of order and part of the institutional structure ensuring that younger citizens refrain from violence toward elders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shame and fear as guardians against violence
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two guardians, shame and fear, mighty to prevent [the younger] from laying hands on those who are in the relation of parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shame prevents disrespect; fear of succour by the injured party's kin deters violence. These social emotions function as institutional checks without reliance on private vengeance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws must enable citizens to keep the peace
rubrics_metrics.description: Then in every way the laws will help the citizens to keep the peace with one another?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws are conceived as designed to secure public tranquillity; the text emphasizes institutional design so private resentments are discharged immediately and do not escalate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common way of life for guardians (common education, children)
rubrics_metrics.description: Men and women are to have a common way of life such as we have described—common education, common children; and they are to watch over the citizens in common whether abiding in the city or going out to war
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared education and communal child-rearing are proposed to bind guardians together, eliminate class self-interest, and produce unity of purpose among protectors of the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women share with men in public duties (while preserving natural relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Always and in all things, as far as they are able, women are to share with the men? And in so doing they will do what is best, and will not violate, but preserve the natural relation of the sexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women are to participate alongside men in education, military service, and civic duties to the extent of their capacities; this equality is framed as compatible with natural differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children should be spectators and trainees of war under safety
rubrics_metrics.description: This then must be our first step,—to make our children spectators of war; but we must also contrive that they shall be secured against danger; then all will be well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children should be exposed to military practice as observers and helpers to learn duties early, but protected from actual danger by assigning them to safe expeditions and placing them under veteran commanders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early horsemanship to prepare youth for war and escape
rubrics_metrics.description: We must mount them on horses in their earliest youth, and when they have learnt to ride, take them on horseback to see war: the horses must not be spirited and warlike, but the most tractable and yet the swiftest that can be had.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training children on horses gives them practical familiarity with warfare and provides them 'wings' to escape danger if needed; leaders teach and protect them during such exposures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degradation for cowardice in battle
rubrics_metrics.description: The soldier who leaves his rank or throws away his arms, or is guilty of any other act of cowardice, should be degraded into the rank of a husbandman or artisan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cowardice is punished by demotion to a lower civic station—both as deterrent and as a method of maintaining military discipline and honor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captured soldiers who allow themselves to be taken may be given to the enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: He who allows himself to be taken prisoner may as well be made a present of to his enemies; he is their lawful prey, and let them do what they like with him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harsh consequences for surrender are proposed to encourage steadfastness; this is presented as an accepted wartime fate for those who fail in duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public honors and tangible rewards for distinguished bravery
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero who has distinguished himself... shall receive honour in the army from his youthful comrades; every one of them in succession shall crown him... receive the right hand of fellowship... be kissed by them... shall have more wives than others... first choices in such matters... and will be honoured with hymns, seats of precedence, meats and full cups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ceremonial honors, social privileges, and material distinctions are tools to recognize and train bravery; they increase incentive to valorous conduct and expand the citizenry by rewarding procreation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor and ceremonial treatment of glorious dead and the exceptionally good
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man dies gloriously in war... he is of the golden race... they are holy angels upon the earth... We must learn of the god how we are to order the sepulture of divine and heroic personages... and in ages to come we will reverence them and kneel before their sepulchres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special burial rites and lasting reverence for heroic or pre-eminently good persons are part of civic religion and moral education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hellenes should not enslave fellow Hellenes; spare kinsmen
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think it right that Hellenes should enslave Hellenic States... Should not their custom be to spare them, considering the danger which there is that the whole race may one day fall under the yoke of the barbarians?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A policy of mutual restraint among Hellenes is recommended to preserve solidarity against external (barbarian) threats—political and cultural unity prioritized over internecine enslavement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbearance toward the slain: no plunder of corpses; don't hinder burial
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not the practice of despoiling an enemy afford an excuse for not facing the battle?... Then we must abstain from spoiling the dead or hindering their burial?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robbing corpses encourages cowardice and is morally mean; forbidding such acts preserves dignity and discourages profiteering from war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid offering Hellenic spoils at temples (risk of pollution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither shall we offer up arms at the temples of the gods, least of all the arms of Hellenes, if we care to maintain good feeling with other Hellenes; and, indeed, we have reason to fear that the offering of spoils taken from kinsmen may be a pollution unless commanded by the god himself?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious practices should not be used to celebrate seizures from kinsmen; this avoids ritual pollution and maintains interstate goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid devastation and burning of Hellenic territory in internal conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Both should be forbidden, in my judgment; I would take the annual produce and no more... when Hellenes fight with one another we shall say that Hellas is then in a state of disorder and discord... such enmity is to be called discord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between 'war' (foreign) and 'discord' (internal); internal conflicts should avoid total devastation, aiming for correction and reconciliation rather than destruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-Hellenic quarrels treated as discord: correctors not enemies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any difference which arises among them will be regarded by them as discord only—a quarrel among friends, which is not to be called a war... They will use friendly correction, but will not enslave or destroy their opponents; they will be correctors, not enemies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal conflicts should aim to reform the guilty few while preserving the innocence of the many; punishments calibrated to secure satisfaction rather than wholesale reprisals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians should be united by family-like bonds and mutual recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: They will all know one another, and each will call the other father, brother, son; and if you suppose the women to join their armies... I know that they will then be absolutely invincible; and there are many domestic advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close social ties among guardians—treating one another as kin—are presented as strengthening cohesion and military effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophers (lovers of the whole) are distinct from lovers of sights/sounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A lover... ought to show his love... not to some one part of that which he loves, but to the whole... the philosopher is a lover, not of a part of wisdom only, but of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True philosophers have a comprehensive appetite for knowledge; mere lovers of appearances or partial arts are imitators and not true philosophers.

rubrics_metrics.name: True philosophers perceive absolute beauty/truth (distinguish idea from objects)
rubrics_metrics.description: He who recognises the existence of absolute beauty and is able to distinguish the idea from the objects which participate in the idea... is wide awake... the mind of the one who knows has knowledge, and the mind of the other, who opines only, has opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The capacity to grasp eternal and immutable Forms (beauty, justice, being) is the epistemic qualification distinguishing rulers who can properly order laws and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge corresponds to being; opinion is intermediate
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is relative to being and knows being... opinion is intermediate between being and not-being; opinion is the faculty concerned with the intermediate 'many' rather than pure being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epistemic taxonomy: rulers must have knowledge (not mere opinion) because knowledge pertains to stable reality required for sound governance; opinion is less reliable and insufficient for guardianship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Those lacking knowledge of true being are 'blind' and unfit as guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who are verily and indeed wanting in the knowledge of the true being of each thing... having perfect vision of the other world to order the laws... are simply blind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers who cannot apprehend the true nature of things cannot properly guard or order the state; epistemic competence is a prerequisite for political authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophic rulers: political greatness must meet the spirit and power of philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Until philosophers are kings, or the kings and princes of this world have the spirit and power of philosophy... cities will never have rest from their evils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reform proposed is singular: combine philosophical knowledge with political rule. Only when rulers are lovers/possessors of wisdom can the ideal state be approximated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish true philosophers from mere lovers of opinion/appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: The lovers of sounds and sights... are fond of fine tones and colours... but their mind is incapable of seeing or loving absolute beauty... Those who love the truth in each thing are to be called lovers of wisdom and not lovers of opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political legitimacy rests on the deeper love of truth; superficial aesthetic or partial tastes do not qualify one for rulership.
